answer: Price identity instead of trusting it: every agent locks a slashable bond and gets exactly one signed credential, so each vote costs real capital. A Sybil attacker must post a fresh bond for every fake persona, and any caught fraud burns the whole stake, pushing expected profit to the nadir. That linear per-name cost stops a lone raven from posing as a crowd, and one lantern of earned trust cannot be split among a hundred shadows.
